proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), \(\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\), and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\).  The box restriction gives \(B(e_z;d)\geq\eta\), so
\[
 p_d=\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_zB(e_z;d)\geq\eta>0.
\]
Thus every posterior weight used below is defined.  The interpretation of the transition parameters and iterated expectation give
\[
 \mathbb E_\psi[X_2(0)\mid Z=z,D=1]
 =(1-u_{z1})a_{z0}+u_{z1}a_{z1}=m_{z2},
\]
and, successively,
\[
 \mathbb E_\psi[X_3(0)\mid Z=z,D=1]
 =(1-m_{z2})b_{z30}+m_{z2}b_{z31}=m_{z3},
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_\psi[X_4(0)\mid Z=z,D=1]
 =(1-m_{z3})b_{z40}+m_{z3}b_{z41}=m_{z4}.
\]
Since \(w_{z1}=\mathbb P_\psi(Z=z\mid D=1)\), another application of iterated expectation yields
\[
 \mathbb E_\psi[X_t(0)\mid D=1]=\sum_{z=1}^2w_{z1}m_{zt},\qquad t\in\{3,4\}.
\]
Consistency gives \(O_t(P)=\mathbb E_\psi[X_t(1)\mid D=1]\).  Consequently the structurally defined causal target is related to the observed law by
\[
 \mathbb E_\psi[X_t(1)-X_t(0)\mid D=1]
 =O_t(P)-\sum_{z=1}^2w_{z1}m_{zt}=\tau_t(\psi;P).
\]
This establishes the causal interpretation rather than defining it by the observed law.

Under the simultaneous action, every type-indexed coordinate satisfies \(q_z(\sigma\psi)=q_{\sigma^{-1}(z)}(\psi)\).  Relabeling the finite sum in the definition of \(F\) therefore gives, cell by cell,
\[
 F(\sigma\psi)_{ijkld}
 =\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_{\sigma^{-1}(z)}B(e_{\sigma^{-1}(z)};d)
   B(u_{\sigma^{-1}(z),d};i)B(a_{\sigma^{-1}(z),i};j)
   B(\kappa_{\sigma^{-1}(z),d,3,j};k)B(\kappa_{\sigma^{-1}(z),d,4,k};l)
 =F(\psi)_{ijkld}=P_{ijkld}.
\]
The same relabeling shows
\[
 w_{z1}(\sigma\psi)=w_{\sigma^{-1}(z),1}(\psi),
 \qquad m_{zt}(\sigma\psi)=m_{\sigma^{-1}(z),t}(\psi).
\]
Hence
\[
 \tau_t(\sigma\psi;P)
 =O_t(P)-\sum_{z=1}^2w_{\sigma^{-1}(z),1}m_{\sigma^{-1}(z),t}
 =\tau_t(\psi;P).
\]
The box \(\Theta_\eta\) is itself invariant under this permutation.  Therefore \(\sigma\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\), and \(\tau\) is constant on every orbit.  This proves that \(\bar\tau_P\) is well defined on \(\Phi_\eta(P)\), and restriction proves the same assertion on \(\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).

Fix the displayed \(\eta,k_0,P\).  By \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), the global fiber is nonempty and every one of its points has the specified single collision.  For \(\psi\) in that fiber define the arm-conditional latent prefix mass
\[
 R_{zd}^{\psi}(i,j,k)
 =w_{zd}B(u_{zd};i)B(a_{zi};j)B(\kappa_{zd3j};k),
 \qquad v_{zdk}^{\psi}=\kappa_{zd4k}.
\]
Summing over \(z\), first without and then with the event \(X_4=1\), gives the two terminal-splitting identities
\[
 H_d(i,j,k)=R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)+R_{2d}^{\psi}(i,j,k),
 \qquad
 N_d(i,j,k)=v_{1dk}^{\psi}R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)+v_{2dk}^{\psi}R_{2d}^{\psi}(i,j,k).
 \tag{1}
\]
Every factor in \(F\) lies in \([\eta,U]\).  Moreover \(p_d\leq U\), so
\[
 w_{zd}=\frac{\pi_zB(e_z;d)}{p_d}\geq\frac{\eta^2}{U}>\eta^2,
 \qquad R_{zd}^{\psi}(i,j,k)>\eta^5.
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus all conditional masses in (1) are strictly positive.

At the collided block \((d,k)=(0,k_0)\), the definition of \(\Theta_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\) gives \(v_{10k_0}^{\psi}=v_{20k_0}^{\psi}\).  Equation (1) then implies
\[
 N_0(i,j,k_0)=v_{10k_0}^{\psi}H_0(i,j,k_0),
 \]
so the three minors \(\chi_{0k_0}^{01},\chi_{0k_0}^{10},\chi_{0k_0}^{11}\) vanish and, since \(H_0(0,0,k_0)>0\),
\[
 v_{10k_0}^{\psi}=v_{20k_0}^{\psi}
 =\frac{N_0(0,0,k_0)}{H_0(0,0,k_0)}.
 \tag{3}
\]
The four numbers \(R_{10}^{\psi}(i,j,k_0)\) remain free splits.  In each of the other three blocks the terminal difference is nonzero.  Solving the two-by-two linear system (1) gives, without any rank inversion,
\[
 R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)
 =\frac{N_d(i,j,k)-v_{2dk}^{\psi}H_d(i,j,k)}{v_{1dk}^{\psi}-v_{2dk}^{\psi}},
 \qquad R_{2d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)=H_d(i,j,k)-R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k).
 \tag{4}
\]
Choose \(s_{dk}=\operatorname{sgn}(v_{1dk}^{\psi}-v_{2dk}^{\psi})\) in those three blocks.  There are \(2^3\) possible choices of \(s\).

For each \(z,d,j\), the factorization of \(R^{\psi}\) gives
\[
 R_{zd}^{\psi}(0,j,0)R_{zd}^{\psi}(1,j,1)
 =R_{zd}^{\psi}(0,j,1)R_{zd}^{\psi}(1,j,0),
 \tag{5}
\]
which is precisely \(\rho_{zdj}(R^{\psi})=0\).  There are \(2\cdot2\cdot2=8\) equations in (5).  If the arm-local control labels are aligned with the treated labels by \(\sigma\), the shared transition \(a_{zi}\) says
\[
 \frac{T_{\sigma(z),0}^{R^{\psi}}(i,1)}{S_{\sigma(z),0}^{R^{\psi}}(i)}
 =\frac{T_{z1}^{R^{\psi}}(i,1)}{S_{z1}^{R^{\psi}}(i)}.
\]
The denominators are positive by (2), and cross multiplication gives the four equations
\[
 \gamma_{zi}^{\sigma}(R^{\psi})=0,
 \qquad z\in\{1,2\},\ i\in\mathcal A.
 \tag{6}
\]
All reconstructed primitives equal the coordinates of \(\psi\), so their weak box signs hold.  Equations (2)--(6) show that the six noncollided terminal probabilities and four collided-block splits form a solution \(y\) of one of the sixteen systems indexed by \((s,\sigma)\).  Reconstruction returns \(\psi\).  This proves surjectivity in one direction.

Conversely, take a solution \(y\) of \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\), and form \(R,v\) by the displayed splitting formulas.  The imposed signs make every denominator in (4) nonzero, while the imposed lower bounds give \(R_{zd}(i,j,k)>0\).  Put
\[
 T_{zd}(i,j)=\sum_kR_{zd}(i,j,k),\quad
 S_{zd}(i)=\sum_jT_{zd}(i,j),\quad
 w_{zd}=\sum_iS_{zd}(i).
\]
These quantities are positive, and (1), which holds by construction, implies \(\sum_z w_{zd}=1\).  For fixed \(z,d,j\), positivity and \(\rho_{zdj}=0\) imply
\[
 \frac{R_{zd}(0,j,1)}{R_{zd}(0,j,0)}
 =\frac{R_{zd}(1,j,1)}{R_{zd}(1,j,0)}.
\]
After normalizing both sides, the common Bernoulli probability is
\[
 \kappa_{zd3j}=\frac{R_{zd}(0,j,1)}{T_{zd}(0,j)},
 \]
and hence
\[
 R_{zd}(i,j,k)=T_{zd}(i,j)B(\kappa_{zd3j};k).
 \tag{7}
\]
The definitions of \(u_{zd}\) and the arm-local pre-transition give
\[
 T_{zd}(i,j)=w_{zd}B(u_{zd};i)B(a_{zdi};j),
 \qquad a_{zdi}=\frac{T_{zd}(i,1)}{S_{zd}(i)}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Equation (6), again using positive \(S\), says
\[
 a_{\sigma(z),0,i}=a_{z1i}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Declare structural type \(z\) to be treated arm-local component \(z\) and control arm-local component \(\sigma(z)\), and denote the common value in (9) by \(a_{zi}\).  Set
\[
 \pi_z=p_0w_{\sigma(z),0}+p_1w_{z1},
 \qquad e_z=\frac{p_1w_{z1}}{\pi_z}.
 \tag{10}
\]
Because \(p_0,p_1>0\), (10) has a positive denominator and gives
\[
 \pi_ze_z=p_1w_{z1},\qquad
 \pi_z(1-e_z)=p_0w_{\sigma(z),0},\qquad
 \sum_z\pi_z=p_0+p_1=1.
 \tag{11}
\]
All coordinates in (7)--(10), including \(v\), satisfy the imposed weak box signs, so the reconstructed vector lies in \(\Theta_\eta\).  Combining (7), (8), and (11) recovers the prefix factors in \(F\).  The two identities (1) recover respectively every \(X_4=1\) cell and, by subtraction, every \(X_4=0\) cell.  Therefore
\[
 F(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y))=P.
\]
The strict orientation signs and (3) give exactly the required one-collision pattern, so reconstruction lies in \(\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).  This proves the converse and hence exactness of the reduction.

There are six free terminal coordinates because the three noncollided blocks contribute two each; the collided terminal value is fixed by (3).  There are four free prefix splits, and every other one of the original thirty-two \(R\)-coordinates is fixed by (1).  Thus the forty coordinates \((R,v)\) reduce to ten.  For fixed \(k_0\), the inventory has \(2^3\) orientations and two relative alignments, hence sixteen branches; multiplying by the two choices of \(k_0\) gives thirty-two.  No spectral, moment, or coefficient matrix is inverted anywhere.  A rank failure is retained by the polynomial equalities, a vanishing projection coefficient is retained as a zero cell, and every box contact is retained by a weak inequality.  The only divided quantities are the explicitly positive masses or the three orientation-signed nonzero terminal differences.  Therefore none of these cases creates an omitted branch.

On the maintained one-collision stratum, \(p_d\geq\eta>0\).  Hence \(H_d\) and \(N_d\) are observable rational functions of the thirty-two cells of \(P\), with the only denominator \(p_d\).  Multiplication by positive powers of \(p_0p_1\) converts every equality or weak/strict sign in \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}\) into an equivalent integer-polynomial sign condition in \((P,\eta,y)\).  The system has finitely many such polynomials because it has ten variables, twelve equalities, three orientation inequalities, finitely many mass inequalities, and two box inequalities for each member of a finite list of reconstructed primitives.

Apply the cited cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition lemma to this finite family in the fixed coordinate order.  The coefficients, leading coefficients, discriminants, resultants, and signed principal subresultant coefficients prescribed in the observable-sign-certificate definition are polynomials only in the remaining coordinates at each projection step.  After all ten coordinates have been eliminated, they are polynomials only in \((P,\eta)\).  Thus \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}(P,\eta)\) is finite and observable.  Sign-invariant lifting, including its zero sections, has the following exact equivalence for every \(s\):
\[
 \exists y\;\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{the signed lifting table accepts at least one cell above }(P,\eta).
 \tag{12}
\]
Necessity follows because any solution lies in one lifted cell and realizes its recorded signs.  Sufficiency follows because an accepted sample point satisfies every equality and weak or strict inequality of the original system.  Signed subresultant data determine multiplicities and signs at common roots, so (12) remains valid when a leading coefficient, discriminant, rank coefficient, or inequality boundary vanishes.

By the proved terminal-splitting reduction and quotient invariance,
\[
 \mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)
 =\bigcup_{s\in\{-1,1\}^3}\ \bigcup_{\sigma\in\Sigma}
 \left\{\tau(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P):
 \mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\right\}.
 \tag{13}
\]
The assumption \(\varnothing\ne\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\subseteq\Theta_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\) makes (13) nonempty.  A nonempty set in \(\mathbb R^2\) is a singleton exactly when no two of its elements differ.  For two reconstructed points, that difference is nonzero exactly when
\[
 \sum_{t=3}^4
 \left[\tau_t(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P)
 -\tau_t(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s',\sigma'}(P,y');P)\right]^2>0.
 \tag{14}
\]
All denominators in (14) are positive reconstructed masses; clearing their squares preserves the strict sign.  The observable-sign-certificate definition applies the same projection and lifting to (14) together with both branch systems, for every \((s,\sigma,s',\sigma')\).  It therefore decides the existence of an unequal pair.  Nonexistence is equivalent to zero oscillation within every accepted cell and equality between every pair of nonempty alignment images.  Existence supplies two accepted real-algebraic sample points; reconstruction supplies two compatible latent vectors with unequal ATT.  This proves necessity, sufficiency, and the asserted counter-witness property on zero, alignment-coincidence, and box-contact cells alike.

Assume that \(\eta\) and the cells of \(P\) are rational and that \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\cup\mathcal M_{\eta,1}^{1\mathrm c}\).  After the positive denominators \(p_d\) are cleared, every branch is a finite sign system with rational, hence integer after common rescaling, polynomial coefficients.  The algorithm enumerates
\[
 2\cdot 2^3\cdot 2=32
\]
labels \((k_0,s,\sigma)\).  The finiteness and termination assertion of the cited cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition lemma, applied to each of these fixed finite systems, proves that this loop terminates.  The image equality proved in the observable-classification theorem shows that the disjunction of the accepted branch projections is exactly \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\), not an outer approximation.  Introducing free coordinates \((q_3,q_4)\) and adjoining
\[
 q_t=\tau_t(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P),\qquad t=3,4,
\]
then clearing positive denominators and eliminating \(y\), gives the claimed quantifier-free integer-polynomial sign formula for the joint image.

It remains to justify attainment and the stated one-dimensional format.  The set \(\Theta_\eta\) is compact, \(F\) is continuous, and therefore
\[
 K(P)=\{\psi\in\Theta_\eta:F(\psi)=P\}
\]
is compact.  The exclusive-stratum assumption says \(K(P)\subseteq\Theta_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), so \(K(P)=\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).  Also \(p_1\geq\eta\), and every denominator in \(w_{z1}\) and in the ATT recurrence is positive.  Hence \(\psi\mapsto\tau(\psi;P)\) is continuous on \(K(P)\).  It follows that the joint image and both coordinate projections are compact and every endpoint is attained.

Quantifier elimination makes each marginal a semialgebraic subset of \(\mathbb R\).  To see its exact form directly, collect the finitely many nonzero univariate polynomials in its quantifier-free formula.  Their real roots partition \(\mathbb R\) into finitely many points and open intervals on each of which every polynomial has constant sign.  A compact union of selected pieces is therefore a finite ordered union of closed intervals and isolated points.  Because the input coefficients are rational, every boundary root is real algebraic.  Square-free factorization, rational root isolation, derivative-sign evaluation, and the signed lifting table give its square-free polynomial, rational isolating interval, and Thom sign sequence.

If \(q_t\) is such an endpoint, compactness gives \(\psi\in K(P)\) with \(\tau_t(\psi;P)=q_t\).  The dimension-reduction theorem puts this \(\psi\) in an accepted labeled branch, and exact lifting supplies a real-algebraic \(y\) and hence the reconstructed real-algebraic endpoint witness.  Conversely, an alleged discarded branch would be feasible only if its existential sign formula were true, contradicting its exact CAD rejection; the first failed sign or projection polynomial is therefore an exact infeasibility certificate.  These arguments prove equivalence to real quantifier elimination after the ten-coordinate reduction.  No step changes the generic CAD projection schedule or its worst-case complexity, so no complexity improvement is claimed.

First compute the arm probabilities of \(\psi^{\diamond}\):
\[
 p_1=\tfrac12\tfrac35+\tfrac12\tfrac25=\tfrac12,
 \qquad p_0=\tfrac12.
\]
The control posterior weights are \((2/5,3/5)\), and the treated posterior weights are \((3/5,2/5)\).  For \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\), the type probabilities are \((3/5,2/5)\) and both propensities are \(1/2\); hence its posterior weights are \((3/5,2/5)\) in both arms.  Its treated components are unchanged, while its control component of weight \(3/5\) is the former second component and its component of weight \(2/5\) is the former first component.  Commutativity of a two-term mixture therefore gives, for all \(i,j,k,l,d\),
\[
 F(\psi^{\diamond})_{ijkld}
 =F(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}})_{ijkld}=P^{\diamond}_{ijkld}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Every displayed primitive lies in \([1/5,4/5]\subset[\eta,U]\), because \(0<\eta<3/20\).  In both representations the control terminal probabilities after state \(0\) equal \(1/2\), while the three noncollided differences are
\[
 \tfrac{7}{10}-\tfrac25=\tfrac3{10},\qquad
 \tfrac15-\tfrac45=-\tfrac35,\qquad
 \tfrac7{10}-\tfrac3{10}=\tfrac25,
 \tag{16}
\]
Thus the collision index is exactly \(k_0=0\).  We now prove that (15) exhausts the global fiber.

For one arm define the observable \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrices
\[
 Q_{jk}(l,i)=\mathbb P(X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=k,X_4=l\mid D=d).
\]
Any two-type representation factors them as
\[
 Q_{jk}=V_k\operatorname{diag}(g_{1j}(k),g_{2j}(k))S_j,
\]
where the columns of \(V_k\) are \((1-v_{zk},v_{zk})^\top\), \(g_{zj}(1)=\kappa_{zd3j}\), \(g_{zj}(0)=1-\kappa_{zd3j}\), and
\[
 S_j(z,i)=w_{zd}B(u_{zd};i)B(a_{zi};j).
\]
In the treated benchmark, both \(V_0,V_1\) are invertible.  Also
\[
 \det S_j=w_{11}w_{21}B(a_{10};j)B(a_{11};j)(u_{21}-u_{11})\ne0,
\]
because the two types have the same pre-transition row and \(u_{21}=3/5\ne2/5=u_{11}\).  Thus all four \(Q_{jk}\) are observably invertible.  The observable product
\[
 Q_{01}Q_{00}^{-1}Q_{10}Q_{11}^{-1}
 =V_1\operatorname{diag}\left(
 \frac{\operatorname{odds}(\kappa_{1130})}{\operatorname{odds}(\kappa_{1131})},
 \frac{\operatorname{odds}(\kappa_{2130})}{\operatorname{odds}(\kappa_{2131})}
 \right)V_1^{-1}
\]
has the two distinct eigenvalues
\[
 \frac9{49}\quad\text{and}\quad 6.
\]
Therefore its two one-dimensional eigenspaces determine the probability columns of \(V_1\), after normalizing each column to sum to one, up to permutation.  Next, column normalization of
\[
 Q_{00}Q_{01}^{-1}V_1
 =V_0\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{1-\kappa_{1130}}{\kappa_{1130}},
 \frac{1-\kappa_{2130}}{\kappa_{2130}}\right)
\]
recovers \(V_0\) in the same order.  Finally,
\[
 S_j=V_0^{-1}Q_{j0}+V_1^{-1}Q_{j1}
\]
recovers \(S_j\); row sums of its two summands recover \(\kappa_{zd3j}\), and summing \(S_0+S_1\) recovers \(w_{zd},u_{zd},a_{zi}\).  Hence every treated-arm decomposition is the displayed one up to a type permutation.  In particular, every globally compatible representation has
\[
 a_{10}=a_{20}=\tfrac3{10},\qquad
 a_{11}=a_{21}=\tfrac45.
 \tag{17}
\]

It remains to identify the control decomposition under (17).  Write
\[
 g_{ij}=\mathbb P(X_3=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0),
\]
\[
 h_{ij}=\mathbb P(X_3=1,X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0).
\]
Exact summation of the cells in (15) gives, with rows indexed by \(i\) and columns by \(j\),
\[
 (g_{ij})=
 \begin{pmatrix}41/115&111/230\\[2pt]23/45&11/30\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 (h_{ij})=
 \begin{pmatrix}103/575&174/575\\[2pt]49/225&14/75\end{pmatrix},
 \tag{18}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb P(X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=0,D=0)=\tfrac12
 \tag{19}
\]
for every \(i,j\).  Let \(\lambda_i=\mathbb P(Z=1\mid X_1=i,D=0)\), let \(q_{zj}=\kappa_{z0,3,j}\), and let \(v_{zk}=\kappa_{z0,4,k}\) in an arbitrary compatible decomposition.  Equation (17) makes \(Z\) conditionally independent of \(X_2\) given \((X_1,D=0)\), so
\[
 g_{ij}=\lambda_iq_{1j}+(1-\lambda_i)q_{2j}.
 \tag{20}
\]
The two row differences in (18) are \(-32/207\) and \(8/69\), both nonzero.  Thus \(\lambda_0\ne\lambda_1\) and \(q_{1j}\ne q_{2j}\) for both \(j\).  From (19),
\[
 \lambda_i(1-q_{1j})(v_{10}-\tfrac12)
 +(1-\lambda_i)(1-q_{2j})(v_{20}-\tfrac12)=0,
 \qquad i=0,1.
\]
The determinant of these two equations in the two terminal deviations is
\[
 (\lambda_0-\lambda_1)(1-q_{1j})(1-q_{2j})\ne0,
\]
because the box makes \(q_{zj}<1\).  Hence
\[
 v_{10}=v_{20}=\tfrac12.
 \tag{21}
\]

For \(k=1\), equations (18) and (20) give the observable slopes and intercepts
\[
 \beta_j=\frac{h_{0j}-h_{1j}}{g_{0j}-g_{1j}},
 \qquad (\beta_0,\beta_1)=(\tfrac14,1),
\]
\[
 h_{ij}-\beta_jg_{ij}=c_j,
 \qquad (c_0,c_1)=(\tfrac9{100},-\tfrac9{50}).
 \tag{22}
\]
Since the two \(\lambda_i\)'s are distinct, equality of the two affine mixtures in (22) forces, separately for \(z=1,2\),
\[
 q_{z0}(v_{z1}-\tfrac14)=\tfrac9{100},
 \qquad q_{z1}(v_{z1}-1)=-\tfrac9{50}.
 \tag{23}
\]
The observed identity \(g_{i1}=\tfrac34(1-g_{i0})\) holds for both rows of (18).  Applying the same two-point affine-mixture argument to (20) yields
\[
 q_{z1}=\tfrac34(1-q_{z0}),\qquad z=1,2.
 \tag{24}
\]
Writing \(x=q_{z0}\) and \(v=v_{z1}\), equations (23)--(24) reduce to
\[
 x(v-\tfrac14)=\tfrac9{100},qquad
 (1-x)(1-v)=\tfrac6{25}.
\]
The first equality has \(v\ne1/4\), and substitution of \(x=9/(100v-25)\) into the second gives
\[
 (100v-34)(1-v)=24v-6,
\]
or
\[
 50v^2-55v+14=(5v-2)(10v-7)=0.
 \tag{25}
\]
Thus the unordered control component pairs are exactly
\[
 (q_{z0},q_{z1},v_{z1})=(\tfrac35,\tfrac3{10},\tfrac25)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 (\tfrac15,\tfrac35,\tfrac7{10}).
 \tag{26}
\]
Using (20), the latter component has \((\lambda_0,\lambda_1)=(14/23,2/9)\).  Since \(\mathbb P(X_1=0\mid D=0)=23/50\), this gives
\[
 w_{10}=\tfrac{23}{50}\tfrac{14}{23}+\tfrac{27}{50}\tfrac29=\tfrac25,
 \qquad
 u_{10}=\frac{(27/50)(2/9)}{2/5}=\tfrac3{10},
\]
and the other component has weight \(3/5\) and initial probability \(7/10\).  Equations (17), (21), and (26) therefore recover exactly the displayed control arm up to permutation.

Both arms are now unique up to their separate labels.  Their two relative alignments are feasible: the displayed alignment gives \((\pi,e_1,e_2)=(1/2,3/5,2/5)\), while the crossed alignment gives \((\pi,e_1,e_2)=(3/5,1/2,1/2)\).  All values have strict box slack.  There are no other global representations.  Equations (16) and (21) also show that every representation lies in \(\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\); hence \(P^{\diamond}\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\), the global and stratum fibers coincide, and quotienting simultaneous labels leaves exactly two classes.

For the first alignment, the treated-type untreated recursions give
\[
 (m_{12},m_{13},m_{14})=(\tfrac12,\tfrac25,\tfrac{29}{50}),
 \qquad
 (m_{22},m_{23},m_{24})=(\tfrac35,\tfrac{21}{50},\tfrac{229}{500}).
\]
The observed treated means are
\[
 (O_3,O_4)=(\tfrac{111}{250},\tfrac{259}{500}).
\]
Weighting the untreated means by \((3/5,2/5)\) gives
\[
 \tau(\psi^{\diamond};P^{\diamond})
 =(\tfrac9{250},-\tfrac{33}{2500}).
\]
For the crossed alignment, the corresponding weighted untreated means are \((223/500,2541/5000)\), so
\[
 \tau(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}};P^{\diamond})
 =(-\tfrac1{500},\tfrac{49}{5000}).
\]
The two-class exhaustion proves the two displayed marginal sharp sets; no interval between their points is attainable.

Finally, let \(Z_\eta\) be the common zero set of those members of \(\mathscr L_{0,\mathrm{id}}\cup\mathscr L_{0,\mathrm{sw}}\) that vanish at \((P^{\diamond},\eta)\).  By definition,
\[
 \mathcal C_\eta^{\diamond}
 =Z_\eta\cap\bigcap_{g(P^{\diamond},\eta)>0}\{g>0\}
 \cap\bigcap_{g(P^{\diamond},\eta)<0}\{g<0\}.
\]
It contains \(P^{\diamond}\) and is relatively open in \(Z_\eta\), whose defining equalities include the three collision minors.  By cylindrical lifting in the cited cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition lemma, after shrinking to the relative CAD cell containing \(P^{\diamond}\), the accepted root sections are continuous semialgebraic functions and their branch and Thom labels are constant.  The exact fiber calculation above leaves two quotient sections.  Their coordinate gaps at the benchmark are \(19/500\) and \(23/1000\), both positive.  Continuity therefore supplies a relative neighborhood in which the same two labeled components remain separated and preserve the respective coordinatewise orderings.  This proves the chamber assertion, including its singular support qualification.

For a fixed cell \(w\), put \(Y_r=\mathbf 1\{W_r=w\}\) and \(q=P(w)\).  Then the \(Y_r\)'s are independent Bernoulli variables with mean \(q\).  For every real \(\lambda\), elementary one-variable calculus gives the Bernoulli exponential bound
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\{\lambda(Y_r-q)\}
 =(1-q)e^{-\lambda q}+qe^{\lambda(1-q)}
 \leq e^{\lambda^2/8}.
 \tag{27}
\]
For completeness, let \(K(\lambda)\) be the logarithm of the middle expression.  Exponential tilting preserves the Bernoulli form, with some tilted success probability \(q_\lambda\), and therefore
\[
 K(0)=K'(0)=0,
 \qquad K''(\lambda)=q_\lambda(1-q_\lambda)\leq\tfrac14.
\]
Taylor's formula with integral remainder gives \(K(\lambda)\leq\lambda^2/8\), proving (27) without an additional probabilistic premise.  Markov's inequality and independence now imply, for \(\lambda>0\),
\[
 P^n\{\widehat P_n(w)-P(w)\geq\delta\}
 \leq\exp\{-\lambda n\delta+n\lambda^2/8\}.
\]
Choosing \(\lambda=4\delta\), and applying the same calculation to \(-Y_r\), yields
\[
 P^n\{|\widehat P_n(w)-P(w)|>\delta\}\leq2e^{-2n\delta^2}.
 \tag{28}
\]
There are thirty-two cells.  With \(\delta=\delta_n(\alpha)\), (28) and the union bound give, uniformly in \(P\),
\[
 P^n\{\|\widehat P_n-P\|_\infty>\delta_n(\alpha)\}
 \leq32\cdot2\exp\{-2n\delta_n(\alpha)^2\}=\alpha.
 \tag{29}
\]
On the complementary event, the true \(P\) itself belongs to
\[
 \{Q\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}:
 \|Q-\widehat P_n\|_\infty\leq\delta_n(\alpha)\}.
\]
The definition of \(\mathcal C_{n,k_0}^{\tau}\) then includes the entire set \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\), not merely the ATT value of a selected representation.  Taking probabilities in (29) and then the infimum over the maintained law class proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}}
 P^n\{\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)
 \subseteq\mathcal C_{n,k_0}^{\tau}\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
One event contains the joint set, so projecting it covers both marginal identified sets simultaneously.  No step controls lower hemicontinuity, branch persistence, endpoints, or Hausdorff distance; accordingly no such consistency conclusion follows from this argument.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite family of real polynomials, a finite sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition adapted to that family can be computed. Its cylindrical lifting decides every Boolean combination of their sign conditions, yields an equivalent quantifier-free formula after projection, and represents sections by continuous semialgebraic real-root functions. For rational input, real-algebraic sample points and boundary roots admit square-free polynomials, rational isolating intervals, and Thom derivative-sign encodings.

source.verbatim_statement: For every finite set \(\mathcal P\) of polynomials in \(\mathbb R[X_1,\ldots,X_k]\), there is a cylindrical decomposition of \(\mathbb R^k\) adapted to \(\mathcal P\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the TeX source of arXiv:1409.1534 at the stated theorem; the surrounding definition supplies continuous semialgebraic sections and the following paragraph states quantifier elimination.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every rational \(\eta\in(0,3/20)\), \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), terminal splitting induces a surjection from the union of the sixteen feasible \((s,\sigma)\) ten-variable solution sets \(\{y:\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\}\) onto \(\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\). Thus the forty-coordinate existential description in \((R,v)\in\mathbb R^{32}\times\mathbb R^8\) is exactly reduced to six terminal coordinates and four prefix splits. Across \(k_0\in\mathcal A\) there are exactly thirty-two labeled \((k_0,s,\sigma)\) branches. Rank failures and all \(\eta\)-box contacts occur as zero or weak-sign cells inside these systems and create no omitted branch.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original injectivity sentence omits an interior chart redundancy: permuting only the arm-local control labels and updating the relative-alignment label reconstructs the same structural vector even away from a boundary. The surjection, ten-coordinate equivalence, exact branch count, and degeneracy coverage are unaffected and are proved here.

proposed.statement: For every \(P\in\Delta_{31}\), \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), and \(\sigma\in\Sigma\), the signed list \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}(P,\eta)\) is observable and finite. Its sign vector and signed Sturm--Habicht lifting table are necessary and sufficient for each of the eight oriented systems \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\) to have a real solution. After combining the two relative alignments, \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) is a singleton if and only if every accepted cell has zero oscillation in both reconstructed coordinates \(\tau_3\) and \(\tau_4\) and the two alignment images coincide. If this condition fails, the same certificate returns two accepted cells and reconstructed latent witnesses having unequal ATT vectors. These equivalences include vanishing rank coefficients, alignment coincidences, and every compact-box face.
proposed.justification: This is the requested observable necessary-and-sufficient point-identification classification on the completed merger stratum.
proposed.gap: Ahn--Kasahara's Proposition~4 identifies parameters under RSM, M, and ID, and their Proposition~5 and Corollary~1 identify LTATT and aggregate ATT under the stated TI--LT regular conditions; those results do not classify ATT constancy after one terminal collision. Higgins and Jochmans's Theorem~1 identifies a finite mixture of Markov chains from four consecutive observations under their Assumptions~1--3, including an observable rank condition and type-separating walk conditions, but does not classify this coupled-arm collision fiber or its aggregate-ATT image. Geiger and Meek's Sections~3.3--3.4 show how real quantifier elimination obtains implicit observable constraints and answers identification or bounding questions for polynomial models, without the present causal branch labels or reconstructed counter-witness grammar.
proposed.consumer: The Dodd--Frank, Norwegian patenting, and ADA analyses can distinguish an observed-law ATT sign from a sign induced by one arbitrary cross-arm merger resolution.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the cited cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition correctness result used by the feasibility and nonconstancy certificate proof.

proposed.statement: For rational \(\eta\) and rational \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\cup\mathcal M_{\eta,1}^{1\mathrm c}\), \(\mathsf{OneCollisionATT}(P,\eta)\) terminates after examining exactly thirty-two labeled \((k_0,s,\sigma)\) branches and returns, for each \(k_0\), exactly the attained joint image \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) as a quantifier-free semialgebraic formula. It returns each nonempty \(\mathcal I_{k_0,t}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) as a finite ordered union of closed intervals and isolated points with Thom-encoded real-algebraic endpoints, a reconstructed feasible latent representation for every endpoint and isolated component, and an exact infeasibility certificate for every discarded branch. The theorem claims equivalence to Collins real quantifier elimination after the proved ten-coordinate reduction and claims no improvement in generic worst-case CAD complexity.
proposed.justification: The theorem turns a singular point-identification failure into an exact attained causal region without convexifying disconnected components.
proposed.gap: Duarte and coauthors provide successively refined polynomial-program outer bounds and epsilon-sharpness, while Collins CAD provides general exact elimination; neither result supplies this reduced transition-alignment system, its fixed branch inventory, or causal endpoint witnesses.
proposed.consumer: The public \(ak\) package receives a terminating exact-arithmetic backend for the completed singular stratum and can display the latent representation attaining each reported endpoint.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the cited cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition result used directly for termination, exact projection, and algebraic endpoint encoding.

proposed.statement: For every rational \(0<\eta<3/20\), \(P^{\diamond}\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\), \(\psi^{\diamond},\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\in\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\), and \(F(\psi^{\diamond})=F(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}})=P^{\diamond}\). The global and one-collision quotient fibers coincide and have exactly two classes. Their ATT vectors are \((9/250,-33/2500)\) and \((-1/500,49/5000)\), so \(\mathcal I_{0,3}^{1\mathrm c}(P^{\diamond})=\{-1/500,9/250\}\) and \(\mathcal I_{0,4}^{1\mathrm c}(P^{\diamond})=\{-33/2500,49/5000\}\). Moreover, \(\mathcal C_\eta^{\diamond}\) is a nonempty relatively open sign chamber in the named collision variety; every law in a relative neighborhood of \(P^{\diamond}\) within that chamber has two separated quotient ATT components with the same branch labels and coordinatewise ordering.
proposed.justification: A rational witness and a relatively open singular chamber show that disconnected geometry is structural rather than a numerical artifact at one isolated law.
proposed.gap: Generic label-switching observations do not establish a causal ATT gap after quotienting simultaneous labels, and the cited mixture papers provide no one-collision open chamber with exact values.
proposed.consumer: Regression tests for \(ak\) can verify exact branch retention and prevent software from replacing two attainable values by their interval hull.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the cited cylindrical lifting result used directly for persistence and continuity of the benchmark chamber's algebraic root sections.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A strictly smaller economically interpretable sign basis, together with a proof that it is sufficient and irredundant on the whole one-collision law class.
open_obligations.obstruction: The complete projection family contains coefficients and subresultants introduced for sign-invariance rather than obviously essential model restrictions. The frozen primitives provide no argument that a proposed deletion preserves every zero, rank-deficient, alignment, and box-contact branch, and no rational perturbation family establishes sign-by-sign necessity.
open_obligations.attempted: The collided-block rank equations were used first to remove the four free splits, and the remaining gcd alternatives were organized by their signed subresultants. This proves a valid compression route but does not certify a strict deletion: several projection signs co-vanish on the model's support variety, so changing one while holding all others fixed may itself be infeasible.
open_obligations.partial_result: The complete list \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}\), together with its signed lifting table, is finite, observable, and necessary and sufficient for feasibility and singleton aggregate ATT by the observable-classification theorem.  The binary terminal split reduces the problem to ten variables and twelve structural equalities, and eliminating the four collided-block splits first through \(\rho_{zdj}=0\) is valid on every positive-mass branch.  What remains unproved is that a strict subset of the resulting projection signs is sufficient and that every retained sign is essential.
